aliases: headache|sakit ulo|masakit ang ulo|masakit ulo|ulo ko|head pain|migraine|migrena|head ache|tension headache
display_name: Headache
tip_1: Rest in a quiet, dim room and start self-care as soon as symptoms begin.
tip_2: Drink water regularly — mild dehydration commonly worsens headache.
tip_3: A cool cloth on the forehead or gentle neck/shoulder stretches may help.
tip_4: If appropriate for you, use a labeled over-the-counter pain reliever exactly as directed; avoid using pain medicine most days of the week without advice.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care sooner if headache is sudden/severe, with neck stiffness, vision changes, weakness, confusion, vomiting, fever, or after a head injury.

aliases: fever|lagnat|hilanat|mainit ang lawas|high temperature|pyrexia|nagliinig|chills|gininig
display_name: Fever
tip_1: Rest and drink extra fluids (water, ORS, clear broths) to prevent dehydration.
tip_2: Wear light clothing and keep the room cool; a lukewarm sponge bath may help comfort after fever medicine if needed.
tip_3: Check temperature again after a few hours and note other symptoms.
tip_4: Adult fever medicine (as labeled) may be used for comfort if no allergy or medical warning; avoid aspirin in children and teens.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if fever is very high, lasts >3 days, with stiff neck, rash, breathing trouble, confusion, severe pain, seizure, or in infants/pregnant patients.

aliases: cough|ubo|nagaubo|dry cough|productive cough|hacking cough|night cough
display_name: Cough
tip_1: Sip warm caffeine-free fluids (water, tea, caldo) to soothe the throat and loosen mucus.
tip_2: Use honey in warm water for adults/older children if no allergy (not for infants under 1 year).
tip_3: Avoid smoke, strong scents, and dusty areas; prop your head with pillows at night if coughing interrupts sleep.
tip_4: OTC cough medicines are optional and not for young children — treat each symptom separately and follow age/label limits.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if cough lasts >2 weeks, with blood, chest pain, high fever, wheezing, or shortness of breath.

aliases: cold|colds|sipon|trangkaso|flu-like|runny nose|baradong ilong|stuffy nose|sneezing|bahing|sip-on|uri|upper respiratory
display_name: Common cold / runny nose
tip_1: Rest, sleep, and drink plenty of caffeine-free fluids to thin mucus.
tip_2: Saline nose spray/drops or brief steam (not scalding) can ease stuffiness.
tip_3: Blow the nose gently; wash hands often; sneeze into a tissue or elbow.
tip_4: Avoid leftover antibiotics — colds are usually viral; treat each symptom with labeled OTC options only if suitable for your age.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if symptoms worsen after about 10 days, or with difficulty breathing, sudden chest pain, severe vomiting, high fever, or strange/confused behavior.

aliases: sore throat|sakit sa tutunlan|masakit lalamunan|masakit ang lalamunan|tunlan|throat pain|pharyngitis
display_name: Sore throat
tip_1: Gargle with warm salt water several times a day if able.
tip_2: Drink warm fluids and avoid very hot, acidic, or spicy drinks.
tip_3: Use a humidifier or sit in a steamy bathroom briefly to moisten the throat.
tip_4: Rest your voice and consider lozenges/honey for adults if appropriate.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you cannot swallow liquids, have drooling, high fever, rash, or breathing difficulty.

aliases: stomach ache|stomachache|sakit tiyan|masakit tiyan|sakit ang tiyan|abdominal pain|tiyan ko|gastro pain|gas pain
display_name: Stomach ache
tip_1: Eat light bland foods (rice, banana, toast) and avoid greasy/spicy meals for a day.
tip_2: Sip water or ORS slowly; avoid large amounts of soda or coffee.
tip_3: Rest upright after meals; a warm compress on the abdomen may ease mild cramps.
tip_4: Do not take leftover prescription medicines without clinician advice.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe pain, persistent vomiting, blood in stool/vomit, rigid abdomen, pregnancy, or pain with fever.

aliases: diarrhea|diarrhoea|paglibang|taliq|nagaibot|loose stool|frequent bowel
display_name: Diarrhea
tip_1: Start oral rehydration (ORS) or clear fluids frequently in small sips.
tip_2: Continue light foods when able; avoid oily, very sweet, or dairy-heavy meals temporarily.
tip_3: Wash hands after toilet use and before eating to prevent spread.
tip_4: OTC anti-diarrheal medicines are not advised if you have fever or bloody stools — ask a pharmacist/clinician first.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if diarrhea lasts >2 days in children or ~5 days in adults, with blood, high fever, severe pain, dehydration signs, or inability to keep fluids down.

aliases: constipation|matigas ang tae|hirap tumae|stool locked|walang tae
display_name: Constipation
tip_1: Increase water intake through the day unless fluid-restricted by your clinician.
tip_2: Add fiber-rich foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains) gradually.
tip_3: Stay lightly active (walking) to help bowel movement.
tip_4: Do not overuse strong laxatives; ask a pharmacist/clinician if needed.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe pain, vomiting, blood in stool, or no bowel movement for several days with swelling.

aliases: nausea|vomiting|sumerko|nagsusuka|ginagahab|gutom na sakit|queasy
display_name: Nausea / mild vomiting
tip_1: Sip clear fluids slowly (water, ORS, ice chips) rather than drinking quickly.
tip_2: Rest sitting upright; avoid strong smells and greasy foods.
tip_3: Try bland foods later (crackers, toast, rice) once vomiting settles.
tip_4: Avoid alcohol and new medicines unless advised.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if vomiting is persistent, with blood, severe abdominal pain, dehydration, or after a head injury.

aliases: dizziness|dizzy|lipong|nahihilo|hilo|lightheaded|vertigo mild
display_name: Mild dizziness
tip_1: Sit or lie down immediately until the spinning/lightheaded feeling passes.
tip_2: Stand up slowly; hold onto support when rising.
tip_3: Drink water and avoid skipping meals.
tip_4: Rest in a safe place and avoid driving or climbing while dizzy.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden severe dizziness with chest pain, fainting, weakness, speech trouble, or after injury.

aliases: back pain|sakit likod|masakit ang likod|lumbar pain|lower back pain|baywang
display_name: Back pain
tip_1: Avoid heavy lifting and sudden twisting for 24–48 hours.
tip_2: Use brief ice or warm compress packs as comfortably tolerated.
tip_3: Gentle walking and light stretching often help more than full bed rest.
tip_4: Keep good posture when sitting; support the lower back with a small pillow.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for back pain with leg weakness/numbness, loss of bladder/bowel control, fever, or trauma.

aliases: body ache|sakit lawas|masakit ang kalamnan|myalgia|muscle pain|pananakit ng katawan|pamamasa
display_name: Body / muscle ache
tip_1: Rest sore muscles and avoid strenuous exercise until better.
tip_2: Apply a warm compress to tight muscle areas for comfort.
tip_3: Stay hydrated and get adequate sleep.
tip_4: Gentle stretching and slow walking may reduce stiffness.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if pain is severe after injury, with swelling/deformity, or with high fever.

aliases: joint pain|sakit tuhod|sakit kasukasuan|arthralgia|knee pain|ankle pain|shoulder pain
display_name: Mild joint pain
tip_1: Rest the joint and avoid activities that sharply increase pain.
tip_2: Elevate the area if swollen and consider a brief cold pack.
tip_3: Support with a soft wrap only if it does not worsen numbness/tingling.
tip_4: Continue light movement within comfort to prevent stiffness.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for hot swollen joints, inability to bear weight, deformity, or fever with joint pain.

aliases: toothache|sakit ngipin|masakit ang ngipin|dental pain|sakit bagang
display_name: Toothache
tip_1: Rinse with warm salt water and keep the area clean.
tip_2: Avoid very hot, cold, or sugary foods that trigger pain.
tip_3: Use dental floss carefully to remove trapped food if present.
tip_4: OTC pain relief may help temporarily if suitable for you; it is not a cure.
when_to_seek_care: See a dentist promptly for swelling of the face, fever, pus, or pain lasting more than 1–2 days.

aliases: earache|sakit tenga|masakit ang tenga|ear pain|otitis mild
display_name: Mild earache
tip_1: Keep the ear dry; avoid inserting cotton buds or oils into the canal.
tip_2: Apply a warm (not hot) compress outside the ear for comfort.
tip_3: Rest with the painful ear up and take fluids.
tip_4: Do not share earphones while infected/irritated.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe pain, discharge, hearing loss, high fever, or symptoms after swimming/injury.

aliases: eye strain|nasakit mata|masakit ang mata|irritated eyes|red eye mild|mata ko|dry eyes
display_name: Eye strain / mild eye irritation
tip_1: Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
tip_2: Blink often and reduce screen brightness if needed.
tip_3: Use preservative-free lubricating drops if recommended for dry eyes.
tip_4: Avoid rubbing the eyes and wash hands before touching them.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden vision loss, severe pain, light sensitivity, chemical exposure, or injury.

aliases: allergy|allergies|allergic rhinitis|hapong|hapong-hapong|sneeze|bahing|itchy nose|pollen allergy|hay fever
display_name: Mild allergy / itchy nose
tip_1: Rinse nasal passages with saline if available.
tip_2: Stay indoors when dust/pollen is high; keep windows closed if helpful.
tip_3: Wash bedding and avoid known triggers (dust, smoke, pet dander).
tip_4: Non-sedating antihistamines may help if appropriate and used as labeled.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, wheezing, or known severe allergy history.

aliases: rash|red spots|pantal|butol|skin rash|itchy rash mild|urticaria mild
display_name: Mild skin rash / itch
tip_1: Keep the area clean and dry; avoid scratching to prevent infection.
tip_2: Use a gentle fragrance-free moisturizer.
tip_3: Wear loose cotton clothing over the irritated area.
tip_4: Cool compresses can reduce itch; ask a pharmacist about soothing lotions if needed.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for rapidly spreading rash, blistering, fever, facial/lip swelling, or breathing trouble.

aliases: insect bite|kagat ng lamok|kagat|mosquito bite|bug bite|ant bite
display_name: Insect bite
tip_1: Wash with soap and water, then apply a cool compress.
tip_2: Avoid scratching; short clean nails reduce skin breaks.
tip_3: Calamine or pharmacist-advised anti-itch cream may help.
tip_4: Watch for increasing redness, warmth, or pus.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, dizziness after a sting, or signs of serious allergic reaction.

aliases: cut|hiwa|gasgas|abrasion|minor wound|scraped skin|kalmot
display_name: Minor cut / scrape
tip_1: Wash gently with clean water and mild soap.
tip_2: Apply light pressure with a clean cloth if still bleeding.
tip_3: Cover with a clean bandage and change daily or when wet/dirty.
tip_4: Keep tetanus vaccination status in mind for deeper wounds.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for deep cuts, uncontrolled bleeding, numbness, animal bites, or signs of infection.

aliases: burn|paso|minor burn|scald|napaso
display_name: Minor burn
tip_1: Cool under cool running water for about 20 minutes (not ice).
tip_2: Remove tight items near the area early before swelling starts.
tip_3: Cover loosely with a clean non-stick dressing.
tip_4: Do not apply toothpaste, butter, or folk pastes.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for burns on face/hands/genitals, large areas, blisters that break open widely, or electrical/chemical burns.

aliases: fatigue|pagod|lupaypay|low energy|tiredness|panghihina|weakness mild
display_name: Fatigue / tiredness
tip_1: Prioritize sleep (consistent bedtime) and short rest breaks in the day.
tip_2: Drink water and eat regular balanced meals; avoid skipping breakfast.
tip_3: Limit caffeine late in the day and reduce alcohol.
tip_4: Light outdoor walking can improve energy more than total inactivity.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if fatigue is sudden/severe, with chest pain, fainting, unexplained weight loss, or lasts many weeks.

aliases: insomnia|hirap matulog|di makatulog|sleepless|walang tulog
display_name: Trouble sleeping
tip_1: Keep a regular sleep and wake time, including weekends when possible.
tip_2: Avoid screens and heavy meals close to bedtime.
tip_3: Make the room dark, quiet, and comfortably cool.
tip_4: Limit naps to under 30 minutes and not late afternoon.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if insomnia lasts weeks, with severe anxiety/depression, or daytime safety risks (falling asleep while driving).

aliases: menstrual pain|sakit regla|cramps|dysmenorrhea|period pain|masakit ang regla
display_name: Menstrual cramps
tip_1: Use a warm compress on the lower abdomen.
tip_2: Gentle stretching, walking, or rest in a comfortable position may help.
tip_3: Stay hydrated and consider heat + OTC pain relief if suitable for you.
tip_4: Track cycle dates and symptom severity for your next visit.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden severe pelvic pain, unusually heavy bleeding, fainting, pregnancy possibility, or pain not typical for you.

aliases: heartburn|asid|asido|acid reflux|maalsom|nagnaigas|burn chest mild|indigestion acid
display_name: Mild heartburn / acid discomfort
tip_1: Eat smaller meals and avoid lying down for 2–3 hours after eating.
tip_2: Limit spicy, fatty, and highly acidic foods temporarily.
tip_3: Elevate the head of the bed slightly if night symptoms occur.
tip_4: Antacids may help short-term if appropriate and used as labeled.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for chest pressure with sweating, arm pain, shortness of breath, or first-time severe chest pain.

aliases: gas|kabag|bloated|kabag gas|flatulence|distended mild
display_name: Gas / bloating
tip_1: Eat slowly and avoid carbonated drinks for a day.
tip_2: Take a short walk after meals to help gas move.
tip_3: Reduce beans, cabbage, and heavy fried foods temporarily if they trigger you.
tip_4: Sip warm water or herbal tea if you tolerate it.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe progressive bloating with vomiting, no flatus/stool, or intense pain.

aliases: overuse|pagod katawan|masakit pagkatapos trabaho|strain mild|pulled muscle mild
display_name: Mild muscle strain / overuse
tip_1: Use RICE basics: rest, ice briefly, compression if comfortable, elevation when swollen.
tip_2: Return to activity gradually; avoid sudden heavy loads.
tip_3: Gentle range-of-motion exercises within pain limits help recovery.
tip_4: Supportive footwear and good lifting posture prevent repeat strain.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you heard a pop, cannot move the limb, have numbness, or swelling worsens quickly.

aliases: uti mild|masakit when peeing|ardor al orinar|sakit ihi|burning urination mild|frequent urination mild
display_name: Mild urinary irritation
tip_1: Drink extra water unless advised to restrict fluids.
tip_2: Do not delay urination; empty the bladder fully.
tip_3: Avoid irritants (alcohol, caffeine, very spicy foods) for a day or two.
tip_4: Keep genital area clean and dry; wipe front to back.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care promptly for fever, back/flank pain, blood in urine, pregnancy, male patients with symptoms, or symptoms lasting >1–2 days.

aliases: hemorrhoid mild|piles|masakit puwit mild|almoranas mild
display_name: Mild hemorrhoid discomfort
tip_1: Increase fiber and water to soften stools and reduce straining.
tip_2: Avoid sitting for very long periods; take short standing breaks.
tip_3: Warm sitz baths can soothe local irritation.
tip_4: Keep the area clean with water; pat dry gently.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for heavy bleeding, severe pain, prolapsed tissue, or dizziness from blood loss.

aliases: stress|kabalaka|anxiety mild|tense|kabado|worried mild|panic mild not emergency
display_name: Stress / tension
tip_1: Practice slow breathing: inhale 4 seconds, exhale 6 seconds, for a few minutes.
tip_2: Take a short walk or stretch break away from the stressor.
tip_3: Talk with a trusted person and keep a simple worry list to revisit later.
tip_4: Protect sleep, meals, and hydration — basic routines reduce stress intensity.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent help for thoughts of self-harm, inability to function, or panic with chest pain/shortness of breath that feels new or severe.

aliases: dehydration mild|uhaw|tuyong bibig|dry mouth|konting ihi
display_name: Mild dehydration
tip_1: Drink ORS or water regularly in small amounts rather than chugging once.
tip_2: Replace fluids after heat exposure, diarrhea, or heavy sweating.
tip_3: Rest in a cool shaded place.
tip_4: Eat watery fruits (banana, melon) when appetite returns.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for confusion, fainting, no urine for many hours, or inability to keep fluids down.

aliases: motion sickness|sasakyan|hilo sa byahe|seasick
display_name: Motion sickness
tip_1: Sit where motion is least (front seat / over wings) and look at the horizon.
tip_2: Avoid heavy meals and strong smells before travel.
tip_3: Fresh air and limiting screen use while moving can help.
tip_4: Ask a pharmacist about travel tablets if appropriate for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if vomiting is severe with headache/neck stiffness or neurological symptoms.

aliases: sinus|sinusitis|sinus infection|masakit sinuses|pressure sa mukha|facial pressure|congested sinuses|sipon na matagal
display_name: Sinus congestion
tip_1: Drink clear fluids often to keep mucus thin so sinuses can drain.
tip_2: Apply a warm moist cloth to the face several times a day; breathe mild steam (bathroom shower steam — not scalding).
tip_3: Use saline nasal spray several times daily; a clean humidifier can help indoor air.
tip_4: If using OTC decongestant nasal spray, limit to a few days only — longer use can rebound congestion.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if symptoms last >10–14 days, severe headache not eased by pain medicine, fever, vision changes, or facial swelling.

aliases: nosebleed|epistaxis|dugo sa ilong|pagdurugo ng ilong|bleeding nose|nullos dugo
display_name: Nosebleed
tip_1: Sit up, lean slightly forward, and breathe through your mouth — do not tip the head back.
tip_2: Pinch the soft part of both nostrils firmly for a full 10–15 minutes without peeking.
tip_3: You may place a cool compress across the bridge of the nose; avoid packing gauze deep inside.
tip_4: After it stops, avoid blowing/picking the nose and heavy lifting for several hours; saline gel can reduce dryness later.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if bleeding continues after two full pressure attempts, follows a head injury, or you feel faint/weak, or nosebleeds keep recurring.

aliases: sprain|sprained ankle|nabaligtad paa|nastrain|twisted ankle|sakit bukong-bukong|mild sprain
display_name: Mild sprain
tip_1: Rest the injured area and avoid putting full weight on it for 1–2 days if painful.
tip_2: Ice 15–20 minutes at a time (cloth barrier) several times a day during the first 48 hours.
tip_3: Use a snug elastic wrap for light compression if toes stay warm/pink and sensation is normal.
tip_4: Elevate the limb above heart level when possible to limit swelling.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you cannot bear weight, the joint feels unstable/numb, bone pain is severe, or it is not improving after 2–3 days.

aliases: neck pain|sakit leeg|masakit ang leeg|stiff neck mild|torticolis mild
display_name: Mild neck pain
tip_1: Avoid sudden twisting and prolonged phone/computer strain; keep screens at eye level.
tip_2: Apply a warm compress or brief ice pack as comfortably tolerated.
tip_3: Gentle range-of-motion stretches within pain limits often help more than complete immobility.
tip_4: Support the neck with a supportive pillow; avoid stomach sleeping if it worsens pain.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for neck pain with fever, severe headache, weakness/numbness in arms, or after a fall/collision.

aliases: sunburn|paso ng araw|nasunog sa araw|red skin from sun
display_name: Sunburn
tip_1: Get out of the sun and cool the skin with lukewarm water or a cool compress (not ice directly).
tip_2: Moisturize with a gentle lotion; avoid petroleum-heavy greasy products on fresh burns if they trap heat.
tip_3: Drink extra water; loose cotton clothing reduces friction.
tip_4: OTC pain relief may help discomfort if suitable for you; do not pop large blisters.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for extensive blistering, fever, confusion, severe pain, or burns on face/eyes/genitals.

aliases: indigestion|dyspepsia|sakit dibdib after kain|busog na masakit|upset stomach|maalsom tiyan
display_name: Indigestion
tip_1: Eat smaller slower meals; stop eating when comfortably full.
tip_2: Avoid trigger foods (very fatty, spicy, fried) and limit alcohol/caffeine for a day.
tip_3: Stay upright after eating; a short walk can ease fullness.
tip_4: Antacids may help short-term if appropriate and labeled for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for vomiting blood, black stools, unintentional weight loss, or chest pain that could be cardiac.

aliases: flu|influenza|trangkaso malala mild|body flu|flu symptoms
display_name: Flu-like illness (home care)
tip_1: Rest at home and sleep more while contagious symptoms are active.
tip_2: Drink fluids often; use fever/pain medicine only as labeled if needed for comfort.
tip_3: Isolate from higher-risk household members when possible; cover coughs and wash hands.
tip_4: Antibiotics do not treat flu viruses — ask about testing/antivirals early if you are high risk.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, inability to keep fluids down, or symptoms that suddenly worsen.

aliases: mouth ulcer|canker sore|singaw|sakit sa bibig|aphthous ulcer
display_name: Mouth ulcer / canker sore
tip_1: Rinse with warm salt water and avoid acidic/spicy foods that sting.
tip_2: Use a soft toothbrush and keep the mouth clean.
tip_3: Cool soft foods and chilled drinks may feel better.
tip_4: Ask a pharmacist about soothing gels if ulcers are very painful.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if ulcers last >2 weeks, you cannot eat/drink, have high fever, or many ulcers appear suddenly.

aliases: hoarse|paos|nawala boses|laryngitis|lost voice|masakit boses
display_name: Hoarse voice / laryngitis
tip_1: Rest your voice — avoid whispering (it can strain more); speak softly only when needed.
tip_2: Drink warm fluids and humidify the air.
tip_3: Avoid smoke and throat clearing as much as possible.
tip_4: Honey/lozenges may soothe adults if appropriate.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if hoarseness lasts >2–3 weeks, or you have breathing difficulty, coughing blood, or unexplained weight loss.

aliases: pink eye|conjunctivitis|namumula mata|sore eyes mild|mata na may sipon
display_name: Mild pink eye
tip_1: Wash hands often and avoid touching/rubbing the eyes.
tip_2: Do not share towels, pillows, or eye makeup.
tip_3: Cool clean compresses can ease discomfort; discard contact lenses until cleared.
tip_4: Artificial tears may soothe irritation if recommended for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for vision loss, severe pain, light sensitivity, eye injury, or symptoms in a newborn.

aliases: bruise|pasa|black and blue|contusion mild|nagusmok
display_name: Mild bruise
tip_1: Rest the area and elevate if on a limb to limit swelling.
tip_2: Apply a cool pack with a cloth barrier for brief periods in the first day.
tip_3: After 1–2 days, warm compresses may help fading comfort for some people.
tip_4: Avoid massage of a fresh painful bruise.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for bruises after a major fall/blow to the head, unexplained easy bruising, or swelling that expands quickly.

aliases: heat exhaustion mild|init|heat stress|sobra ang init|init ng araw|nauuinit
display_name: Mild heat stress
tip_1: Move to a cool shaded or air-conditioned place right away.
tip_2: Loosen clothing and apply cool wet cloths to the skin.
tip_3: Sip water or ORS slowly if you are fully awake and not vomiting heavily.
tip_4: Rest until sweating and weakness improve.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for confusion, fainting, vomiting that prevents drinking, very hot dry skin, or seizures — possible heat emergency.

aliases: leg cramp|pulikat|charley horse|sakit binti bigla|calf cramp
display_name: Leg cramp
tip_1: Gently stretch and massage the cramped muscle; walk carefully once it eases.
tip_2: Hydrate and ensure you are not skipping meals/electrolytes after heavy sweat.
tip_3: Apply a warm pack after the cramp settles if the muscle remains tight.
tip_4: Review sudden new medicines with a clinician/pharmacist if cramps are frequent.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for swelling/redness in one leg, chest pain, or cramps with severe weakness.

aliases: morning sickness|nausea pregnancy mild|sumerko buntis|pregnancy nausea mild
display_name: Mild pregnancy nausea
tip_1: Eat small frequent bland snacks (crackers) rather than large meals.
tip_2: Sip fluids between meals; ginger tea or hard ginger candy may help some people.
tip_3: Avoid strong smells and greasy foods.
tip_4: Rest and rise slowly from bed.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for inability to keep fluids down, dizziness, weight loss, severe vomiting, or abdominal pain — do not start new medicines without clinician advice.

aliases: food poisoning|sira ang tiyan|kuspad|foodborne mild|agusaw after kain
display_name: Mild food poisoning recovery
tip_1: Focus on ORS/clear fluids first until vomiting settles.
tip_2: Return to bland foods gradually (BRAT-style: banana, rice, apple sauce, toast) when hungry.
tip_3: Rest and avoid dairy, alcohol, and greasy foods for a day or two.
tip_4: Practice careful handwashing and discard leftover suspect food.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for bloody diarrhea, high fever, severe dehydration, or symptoms lasting beyond a couple of days.

aliases: athlete foot|alipunga|itchy feet fungus|foot fungus mild
display_name: Athlete's foot
tip_1: Wash and dry feet carefully, especially between toes.
tip_2: Wear clean dry socks; alternate shoes to let them dry.
tip_3: Over-the-counter antifungal cream may help if used as labeled for the full course.
tip_4: Avoid sharing towels and walking barefoot in damp public areas when possible.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the rash spreads, has pus, severe swelling, fever, or you have diabetes/poor circulation.

aliases: cold sore|herpes labialis|singaw sa labi|fever blister
display_name: Cold sore
tip_1: Avoid kissing/sharing utensils while sores are open.
tip_2: Apply a cool compress; keep the area clean and dry.
tip_3: Ask a pharmacist about topical antiviral creams started early if appropriate.
tip_4: Do not pick the sore; wash hands after touching it.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sores near the eyes, frequent severe outbreaks, or sores with high fever in infants.

aliases: post nasal drip|uhog sa lalamunan|throat mucus|tickle throat mucus
display_name: Post-nasal drip
tip_1: Drink fluids and use saline nasal rinse/spray to thin mucus.
tip_2: Sleep with the head slightly elevated.
tip_3: A clean humidifier may reduce throat tickle from dryness.
tip_4: Avoid smoke; treat allergy triggers if they are known.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if drip lasts weeks with facial pain, green/bloody discharge, fever, or wheezing.

aliases: chest congestion|phlegm sa dibdib|malapot uhog|productive chest mild
display_name: Mild chest congestion
tip_1: Drink warm fluids and rest to help loosen phlegm.
tip_2: Use steamy air carefully; avoid smoke exposure.
tip_3: Honey (adults/older children) may soothe cough; expectorants only if labeled for you.
tip_4: Do not suppress a productive cough completely if mucus is clearing.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for shortness of breath, chest pain, bluish lips, high fever, or coughing blood.

aliases: sciatica|sakit nerbiyos binti|shooting leg pain mild|nerve pain leg mild
display_name: Mild sciatica-like pain
tip_1: Avoid prolonged sitting; take short walking breaks.
tip_2: Use ice or heat packs as comfortable for short sessions.
tip_3: Gentle stretches for hips/hamstrings within pain limits may help.
tip_4: Sleep on a supportive surface; a pillow between knees can reduce strain.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for progressive weakness, numbness in the groin, or loss of bladder/bowel control.

aliases: wrist pain|sakit pulso|carpal strain mild|nastrain kamay
display_name: Mild wrist strain
tip_1: Rest from repetitive straining tasks for 24–48 hours.
tip_2: Ice briefly with a cloth barrier if swollen.
tip_3: A soft wrist support may help daytime tasks if sensation stays normal.
tip_4: Return to typing/lifting gradually with neutral wrist posture.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care after a fall onto the wrist, visible deformity, or numbness that does not improve.

aliases: heel pain|sakit sakong|plantar fasciitis mild|sakit talampakan
display_name: Mild heel pain
tip_1: Reduce high-impact activity for a few days; choose supportive shoes.
tip_2: Gentle calf stretches before standing first thing in the morning may help.
tip_3: Ice the heel briefly after activity if sore.
tip_4: Avoid walking barefoot on hard floors while symptomatic.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for inability to walk, heel bruising after injury, or pain that worsens over weeks.

aliases: dry skin|eczema mild|pagkatuyo ng balat|itchy dry skin|kaliskis balat mild
display_name: Dry skin / mild eczema
tip_1: Moisturize often with fragrance-free cream after bathing.
tip_2: Use lukewarm (not hot) water and gentle cleanser; pat dry.
tip_3: Wear soft cotton layers; avoid known irritants (harsh soaps, wool if triggering).
tip_4: Keep nails short to reduce scratch damage.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for oozing infection, fever, rapidly spreading redness, or severe sleep-disturbing itch.

aliases: dengue|dengue watch|dengue mild watch|possible dengue home|lagnat dengue watch|dengge
display_name: Fever with body pain (dengue-watch home care)
tip_1: Rest and drink ORS/water frequently; monitor urine output.
tip_2: Use acetaminophen/paracetamol only as labeled for fever/pain if suitable — avoid aspirin/ibuprofen if dengue is possible unless a clinician says otherwise.
tip_3: Use mosquito nets/repellent to protect others; eliminate standing water around the home.
tip_4: Watch warning signs closely: severe belly pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums/nose, black stools, restlessness, cold clammy skin.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for any warning signs, fever with bleeding, severe lethargy, or inability to drink — dengue can worsen quickly after the fever drops.

aliases: covid mild|covid-19 home|positive covid mild|corona mild
display_name: Mild COVID-like illness
tip_1: Rest at home, isolate as advised locally, and improve room ventilation when possible.
tip_2: Drink fluids; use labeled fever/pain medicine for comfort if appropriate.
tip_3: Monitor breathing and oxygen needs if you have a pulse oximeter and know your baseline.
tip_4: Contact a clinician early if you are high risk — antivirals work best soon after symptoms start.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, blue lips, or inability to stay awake.

aliases: sore arm after vaccine|baka pain|vaccine side effect mild|masakit braso bakuna
display_name: Mild vaccine arm soreness
tip_1: Move the arm gently through normal range several times a day.
tip_2: A cool compress can ease local soreness.
tip_3: Labeled OTC pain relievers may help if suitable for you.
tip_4: Rest if you feel briefly fatigued; stay hydrated.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for rash with breathing difficulty, high fever lasting days, or arm swelling that rapidly worsens.

aliases: diaper rash|lampin|pulang puwet bata|nappy rash
display_name: Diaper rash
tip_1: Change wet/soiled diapers promptly and clean gently with water.
tip_2: Pat dry and allow short diaper-free air time when practical.
tip_3: Use a thick barrier cream (zinc oxide style) as labeled.
tip_4: Avoid harsh wipes with alcohol/fragrance if they irritate.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for open sores, fever, spreading redness, or rash lasting more than a few days.

aliases: teething|ngingipin|baby teething|sakit gilagid bata
display_name: Teething discomfort
tip_1: Offer a clean cool (not frozen hard) teething ring if age-appropriate.
tip_2: Gently massage the gum with a clean finger.
tip_3: Keep the face dry; drool can irritate the chin — apply a thin barrier cream if needed.
tip_4: Avoid teething gels with benzocaine in young children unless a clinician advises.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for high fever, rash, diarrhea with dehydration, or refusal to drink — teething alone rarely causes high fever.

aliases: hiccups|singultus|solok-solok|hikab hiccup
display_name: Hiccups
tip_1: Sip cold water slowly or hold a brief breath, then exhale gently.
tip_2: Breathe into a paper bag briefly only if safe and not for people with breathing disease.
tip_3: Relax the diaphragm; avoid carbonated drinks and rapid eating for a while.
tip_4: Most hiccup bouts stop on their own within minutes to hours.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if hiccups last >48 hours, interfere with sleep/eating, or follow recent surgery/illness.

aliases: splinter|tinik|aspili sa balat|tuhog kahoy
display_name: Splinter
tip_1: Wash hands and the area with soap and water.
tip_2: Use cleaned tweezers to remove a visible splinter along the entry track.
tip_3: If the tip is under skin, a sterilized needle may help lift it — then wash again.
tip_4: Apply a clean bandage; watch for redness.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the splinter is deep, under a nail, from rusty/dirty metal, or infection signs appear.
resource_label: NHS: How to remove a splinter

aliases: blister|paltos|blister from shoes|paltos paa
display_name: Friction blister
tip_1: Leave intact blisters closed when possible — the skin is a natural bandage.
tip_2: Cover with a clean blister plaster or soft padding to reduce rub.
tip_3: If a blister opens, wash gently and cover with a non-stick dressing.
tip_4: Wear better-fitting socks/shoes to prevent repeat blisters.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for spreading redness, pus, fever, or blisters in people with diabetes/poor circulation.

aliases: loss of appetite|walang gana|reduced appetite mild|ayaw kumain mild
display_name: Mild loss of appetite
tip_1: Offer small frequent easy meals rather than large plates.
tip_2: Choose nutrient-dense soft foods and keep fluids up.
tip_3: Light activity and fresh air before meals may help appetite.
tip_4: Avoid forcing large meals; track weight if appetite stays low.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if appetite loss lasts weeks, with weight loss, fever, vomiting, or severe fatigue.

aliases: gout mild|sakit daliri paa bigla|gouty toe mild|uric acid pain mild
display_name: Mild gout-like joint flare
tip_1: Rest the joint and elevate it; avoid pressure from tight shoes.
tip_2: Ice briefly with a cloth barrier for comfort.
tip_3: Drink water unless fluid-restricted; avoid alcohol during a flare.
tip_4: Do not start new strong pain medicines without advice if kidney disease or ulcers are known.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for hot swollen joint with fever, first-time severe attack, or inability to walk.

aliases: itchy eyes allergy|hapong mata|watery allergic eyes|allergic conjunctivitis mild
display_name: Allergic itchy eyes
tip_1: Avoid rubbing; use cool compresses.
tip_2: Reduce exposure to dust/pollen; wash face and change pillowcases.
tip_3: Preservative-free lubricating drops may soothe; ask about antihistamine eye drops if needed.
tip_4: Wash hands before any eye drop use.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for pain, vision change, thick yellow discharge, or light sensitivity.

aliases: pinworm|bulate sa puwit|anal itch night|enterobius mild
display_name: Suspected pinworm itch
tip_1: Bathe in the morning and change underwear daily.
tip_2: Wash hands after toilet and before meals; keep nails short.
tip_3: Wash bedding/pajamas frequently in hot water when possible.
tip_4: Do not share towels; clean bathroom surfaces.
when_to_seek_care: See a clinician for confirmed treatment — self-medicating worm tablets without advice is not recommended for all ages.

aliases: acne|pimples|tagihawat|blackheads|mild acne|butlig sa mukha
display_name: Mild acne
tip_1: Wash the face gently twice daily with a mild cleanser; do not scrub hard.
tip_2: Avoid picking or squeezing pimples to reduce scarring and infection.
tip_3: Use non-comedogenic moisturizer if skin feels dry from treatments.
tip_4: Ask a pharmacist about benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid products used as labeled.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for painful deep cysts, scarring acne, sudden widespread rash, or acne with fever.

aliases: dandruff|balakubak|flaky scalp|itchy scalp flakes
display_name: Dandruff
tip_1: Wash hair regularly with a gentle shampoo; rinse thoroughly.
tip_2: Try an anti-dandruff shampoo (zinc pyrithione, selenium, or ketoconazole style) as labeled.
tip_3: Avoid scratching the scalp with nails.
tip_4: Do not share combs/hats while flaking is heavy.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the scalp is very red, oozing, swollen, or flakes do not improve after a few weeks of proper shampoo use.

aliases: dry eyes|tuyong mata|gritty eyes|mata tuyo|computer dry eye
display_name: Dry eyes
tip_1: Blink fully and often during screen use; take regular screen breaks.
tip_2: Use preservative-free lubricating (artificial tear) drops if suitable for you.
tip_3: Avoid direct fan/AC blow into the eyes; consider a humidifier indoors.
tip_4: Limit smoke exposure and long contact-lens wear while symptomatic.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden vision change, severe pain, light sensitivity, chemical splash, or redness with discharge.

aliases: earwax|plug tenga|tenga barado|cerumen|blocked ear wax
display_name: Earwax blockage
tip_1: Do not insert cotton buds, hairpins, or oils deep into the ear canal.
tip_2: Ask a pharmacist about pharmacy ear drops to soften wax if appropriate.
tip_3: Keep ears dry; avoid swimming until clearer if the ear feels plugged.
tip_4: Gently wipe only the outer ear with a clean cloth.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe pain, discharge, hearing loss after cleaning attempts, dizziness, or known eardrum perforation.

aliases: contact dermatitis|irritated skin soap|hapong balat contact|allergic contact rash mild|rash from detergent
display_name: Mild contact dermatitis
tip_1: Wash the area with lukewarm water and mild soap; rinse off the trigger if known.
tip_2: Avoid the suspected irritant (new soap, jewelry, plant, detergent).
tip_3: Apply a fragrance-free moisturizer several times a day.
tip_4: Cool compresses can ease itch; ask about 1% hydrocortisone cream for short use if suitable.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for facial/lip swelling, breathing trouble, blistering, rapidly spreading rash, or fever.

aliases: head lice|kuto|lisa|head louse|kuto sa ulo
display_name: Head lice
tip_1: Check family members and treat close contacts as advised on product labels.
tip_2: Use a pharmacy lice treatment exactly as directed; comb wet hair with a fine nit comb.
tip_3: Wash pillowcases, hats, and recently used hair tools in hot water when possible.
tip_4: Avoid sharing combs, brushes, and headphones during treatment.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if scalp is infected (pus, swelling), treatment fails twice, or for infants — confirm age-safe products first.

aliases: ringworm|buni|tinea|circular itchy rash|fungal ring rash
display_name: Ringworm (body)
tip_1: Keep the rash clean and dry; wash hands after touching it.
tip_2: Apply an OTC antifungal cream as labeled for the full course, even after it looks better.
tip_3: Do not share towels, clothes, or sports gear.
tip_4: Cover the area loosely with clean clothing during treatment when practical.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the ring spreads widely, involves the scalp/nails, has pus, or you have diabetes/weak immunity.

aliases: oral thrush|gagamba sa bibig|white patches mouth|candidiasis mouth mild
display_name: Mild oral thrush
tip_1: Rinse the mouth with warm salt water after meals; keep dentures cleaned daily if used.
tip_2: Brush gently and avoid harsh mouthwashes that sting.
tip_3: Reduce sugary snacks temporarily; rinse after inhaler use if you use steroid inhalers.
tip_4: Do not scrape white patches aggressively.
when_to_seek_care: See a clinician for prescription treatment — thrush often needs medicated drops/gel; seek care sooner if swallowing pain or fever.

aliases: hay fever|seasonal allergy|pollen allergy flare|hapong season|allergy season
display_name: Hay fever flare
tip_1: Stay indoors when pollen counts are high; keep windows closed if helpful.
tip_2: Shower and change clothes after outdoor exposure; wash pillowcases more often.
tip_3: Saline nose rinse and cool eye compresses can ease itch.
tip_4: Non-sedating antihistamines may help if appropriate and used as labeled.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for wheezing, chest tightness, facial swelling, or known severe allergy history.

aliases: shoulder pain|sakit balikat|masakit ang balikat|frozen start mild|shoulder strain mild
display_name: Mild shoulder pain
tip_1: Avoid overhead heavy lifting and sudden jerking movements for a few days.
tip_2: Apply ice briefly after activity or heat for stiffness — whichever feels better.
tip_3: Pendulum or gentle range-of-motion exercises within pain limits help prevent freezing.
tip_4: Sleep with a pillow supporting the arm if side-lying worsens pain.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care after a fall/dislocation feeling, arm weakness/numbness, chest pain with shoulder pain, or no improvement in 1–2 weeks.

aliases: knee strain|sakit tuhod after lakad|mild knee sprain|masakit tuhod lakad
display_name: Mild knee strain
tip_1: Rest from running/jumping for 1–2 days; walk short distances as tolerated.
tip_2: Ice 15–20 minutes with a cloth barrier if swollen.
tip_3: Elevate the leg when sitting; a soft brace may help confidence if sensation is normal.
tip_4: Strengthen gradually with straight-leg raises once sharp pain settles.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the knee locks, gives way, is very swollen/hot, or you cannot bear weight.

aliases: tennis elbow|sakit siko|lateral elbow pain|golfer elbow mild|elbow strain
display_name: Mild elbow strain
tip_1: Reduce repetitive gripping/twisting tasks for several days.
tip_2: Ice briefly after activity that aggravates the elbow.
tip_3: Gentle forearm stretches within comfort can help.
tip_4: Check tool/mouse grip size; take micro-breaks during repetitive work.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for elbow deformity after injury, numbness in fingers, or pain that blocks daily tasks for weeks.

aliases: jaw pain|sakit panga|tmj|clicking jaw mild|masakit ngumunguya
display_name: Mild jaw / TMJ discomfort
tip_1: Eat soft foods temporarily; avoid chewing gum and hard candy.
tip_2: Do not force wide yawns; support the jaw when yawning if needed.
tip_3: Apply a warm compress to tight jaw muscles.
tip_4: Practice gentle jaw relaxation; avoid constant teeth clenching.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for inability to open/close the mouth, jaw trauma, fever with swelling, or pain lasting weeks.

aliases: sore gums|sakit gilagid|gingivitis mild|bleeding gums brush
display_name: Mild sore / bleeding gums
tip_1: Brush twice daily with a soft brush and gentle technique; floss carefully once daily.
tip_2: Rinse with warm salt water after meals.
tip_3: Avoid smoking and very sticky sweets while gums are inflamed.
tip_4: See a dentist for cleaning if bleeding continues — home care helps but does not replace dental care.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for loose teeth, facial swelling, fever, or gum pain with pus.

aliases: chapped lips|bitak labi|dry cracked lips|labi bitak
display_name: Chapped lips
tip_1: Apply a plain lip balm or petroleum jelly often, including before sleep.
tip_2: Drink water regularly; avoid constant licking of the lips.
tip_3: Use a humidifier if indoor air is very dry.
tip_4: Choose fragrance-free balms if scented products sting.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for deep painful cracks that bleed a lot, spreading sores, or signs of infection.

aliases: hangover|resaca|hilo after inom|sakit ulo after alcohol|hang over
display_name: Mild hangover
tip_1: Drink water or ORS; rehydrate slowly through the morning.
tip_2: Eat a light bland meal when you can (toast, rice, banana).
tip_3: Rest in a quiet room; cool compress may ease headache.
tip_4: Do not take more alcohol to “cure” a hangover; use labeled OTC pain relief only if suitable and never with leftover unknown pills.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for confusion, vomiting blood, chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or inability to keep fluids down.

aliases: jet lag|pagod byahe|travel fatigue|pagod after biyahe|long trip tired
display_name: Travel fatigue / jet lag
tip_1: Get sunlight in the morning at your destination when safe; keep daytime naps short.
tip_2: Hydrate on travel days; limit alcohol on flights/buses.
tip_3: Align bedtime gradually to local time over 1–2 days.
tip_4: Light walking helps reset energy better than staying in bed all day.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if severe dizziness, chest pain, one-sided leg swelling after long travel, or confusion appears.

aliases: sore feet|sakit paa after tayo|tired feet|masakit talampakan after work
display_name: Sore tired feet
tip_1: Rest and elevate the feet after long standing or walking.
tip_2: Soak briefly in lukewarm water, then moisturize dry skin (not between wet toes if fungal risk).
tip_3: Wear supportive shoes and cushioned socks; rotate footwear.
tip_4: Gentle foot and calf stretches can reduce tightness.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for foot wounds if you have diabetes, sudden swelling in one leg, or inability to walk.

aliases: cracked heels|bitak sakong|heel fissures|basag sakong
display_name: Cracked heels
tip_1: Soak feet in lukewarm water, then gently file thick hard skin — do not cut deep.
tip_2: Apply a thick moisturizer or urea cream as labeled; cotton socks at night can help.
tip_3: Wear closed shoes that support the heel; avoid barefoot on hard floors while deep cracks heal.
tip_4: Keep blood sugar controlled if diabetic — foot care is higher risk.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for deep bleeding cracks, infection signs, or any foot crack if you have diabetes/poor circulation.

aliases: boil|pigsa|folliculitis|early boil|masakit butlig nana
display_name: Early boil / folliculitis
tip_1: Apply warm moist compresses several times a day to encourage drainage naturally.
tip_2: Keep the area clean; do not squeeze or lance the boil at home.
tip_3: Cover with a clean bandage if draining; wash hands after care.
tip_4: Change clothes/towels that touched the drain.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for fever, red streaks, boils on the face/spine, diabetes, or a boil that worsens after 1–2 days.

aliases: charley after hit|pasa kalamnan|dead leg mild|corked thigh mild
display_name: Mild muscle bruise
tip_1: Rest and ice the area with a cloth barrier in the first 24–48 hours.
tip_2: Elevate a bruised limb when possible; avoid deep massage early on.
tip_3: Return to sport gradually once walking is comfortable.
tip_4: Compression wrap only if toes/fingers stay warm with normal color.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for rapidly expanding swelling, numbness, or inability to move the limb.

aliases: asthma mild trigger|hika mild|wheeze trigger avoid|hika alikabok
display_name: Asthma trigger care (stable)
tip_1: Avoid known triggers (smoke, dust, cold air bursts, strong fumes) when possible.
tip_2: Take controller/reliever inhalers exactly as your clinician prescribed — this tip does not replace your action plan.
tip_3: Keep rescue inhaler accessible; sit upright during mild tightness and use your plan.
tip_4: Track peak flow or symptom notes if you were taught to.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for difficulty speaking, blue lips, severe wheeze, or if rescue medicine is not helping — asthma can become an emergency.

aliases: hives|urticaria|pantal bigla|welts|kabag balat allergy
display_name: Mild hives
tip_1: Avoid hot showers and tight clothing over the welts.
tip_2: Cool compresses and a non-sedating antihistamine (if suitable/labeled) may reduce itch.
tip_3: Note possible triggers (food, medicine, infection, heat).
tip_4: Do not scratch open the skin.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for lip/tongue swelling, wheezing, dizziness, or hives with breathing trouble — possible severe allergy.

aliases: throat tickle|halimhim lalamunan|scratchy throat morning|throat clearing
display_name: Scratchy throat from drip
tip_1: Sip warm fluids through the day; honey may soothe adults/older children (not infants).
tip_2: Saline nasal spray at night can reduce morning throat drip.
tip_3: Sleep with the head slightly elevated.
tip_4: Avoid smoke and excessive throat clearing.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you cannot swallow, have high fever, rash, or breathing difficulty.

aliases: constipation child mild|hirap tumae bata|matigas tae bata
display_name: Mild constipation (child home care)
tip_1: Offer water regularly and age-appropriate fruits/vegetables if diet allows.
tip_2: Encourage toilet sitting after meals without pressure or punishment.
tip_3: Keep activity/play going — movement helps bowel habits.
tip_4: Do not give adult laxatives to children unless a clinician advises.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe pain, vomiting, blood in stool, swollen belly, or constipation lasting days with distress.

aliases: oras ors|dehydration diarrhea focus|paglibang needs ors|taliq ors
display_name: Diarrhea — ORS focus
tip_1: Give ORS frequently in small sips after each loose stool when possible.
tip_2: Continue breastfeeding/usual milk for infants as advised; adults may use clear broths too.
tip_3: Avoid sugary sodas and undiluted fruit juice which can worsen diarrhea.
tip_4: Watch for dry mouth, no tears, sunken eyes, or very little urine.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care urgently for blood in stool, high fever, severe lethargy, or dehydration signs — especially in young children.

aliases: night acid|maalsom gabi|reflux at night|gabi asido
display_name: Night-time acid reflux
tip_1: Finish evening meals 2–3 hours before lying down.
tip_2: Elevate the head of the bed slightly; avoid stacking only under the neck.
tip_3: Limit late spicy, fatty, mint, chocolate, and caffeine foods.
tip_4: Sleep on the left side if comfortable — it may reduce night reflux for some people.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for crushing chest pain, sweating, arm pain, or shortness of breath.

aliases: varicose ache|sakit ugat binti|heavy legs veins|masakit ugat paa
display_name: Mild varicose vein ache
tip_1: Elevate the legs when resting; avoid long motionless standing.
tip_2: Walk regularly to keep calf muscles pumping blood.
tip_3: Compression stockings may help if fitted/advised for you.
tip_4: Maintain healthy weight and stay hydrated.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for one-sided swelling/redness/heat (possible clot), skin ulcers, or sudden severe leg pain.

aliases: restless legs|hindi mapakali binti|legs jumpy night|rlsless legs
display_name: Mild restless legs
tip_1: Gentle leg stretches before bed; try a short evening walk.
tip_2: Reduce caffeine late in the day; keep a regular sleep schedule.
tip_3: Warm bath or massage may ease the urge to move for some people.
tip_4: Check with a clinician if symptoms are frequent — iron and other causes may need testing.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe sleep loss, progressive weakness, or swelling/redness in one leg.

aliases: scabies|galis|kati gabi|mite itch night|sarna
display_name: Suspected scabies itch
tip_1: Avoid close skin contact and do not share bedding/clothes until assessed.
tip_2: Wash recently used clothes and sheets in hot water when possible.
tip_3: Keep nails short; try not to scratch open the skin.
tip_4: Do not share home mite creams without guidance — treatment must cover contacts correctly.
when_to_seek_care: See a clinician promptly for diagnosis and proper treatment; seek sooner if infection (pus) appears.

aliases: chickenpox|bulutong tubig|varicella mild home|pox spots
display_name: Chickenpox home care
tip_1: Keep nails short; use cool baths and calamine to reduce itch.
tip_2: Stay home until lesions crust as advised by local public-health/clinician guidance.
tip_3: Acetaminophen/paracetamol may help fever if suitable — avoid aspirin in children/teens.
tip_4: Hydrate and rest; soft foods help if mouth spots hurt.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for breathing trouble, severe headache, vomiting, eye involvement, or high-risk patients (pregnant, newborn, weak immunity).

aliases: measles watch|tigdas watch|possible measles|lagnat with rash measles
display_name: Fever with rash (measles-watch)
tip_1: Rest and drink fluids; isolate from pregnant people, infants, and unvaccinated contacts.
tip_2: Use fever medicine only as labeled if suitable; keep the room dim if eyes are sensitive.
tip_3: Do not give aspirin to children/teens.
tip_4: Note vaccination history for the clinician.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for breathing difficulty, confusion, stiff neck, ear pain with fever, or if measles is suspected — public health advice may be needed.

aliases: hand foot mouth|hfmd|singaw kamay paa|hfmd bata
display_name: Hand-foot-mouth comfort
tip_1: Offer cool soft foods and plenty of fluids; avoid acidic juices if mouth sores sting.
tip_2: Keep hands washed; disinfect shared toys for young children.
tip_3: Use fever/pain medicine only as labeled and age-appropriate.
tip_4: Children usually recover in about a week with rest.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the child cannot drink, has fewer wet diapers, stiff neck, or unusual sleepiness.

aliases: rib pain cough|sakit tadyang pag ubo|chest wall pain cough
display_name: Chest-wall sore from coughing
tip_1: Support the sore side with a pillow when coughing or laughing.
tip_2: Warm compress and gentle posture breaks can ease muscle strain.
tip_3: Continue fluids and cough care; labeled pain relief may help if suitable.
tip_4: Practice slow deep breaths several times a day to reduce shallow-breathing stiffness.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden sharp chest pain with shortness of breath, coughing blood, trauma, or pain at rest that worsens.

aliases: swimmers ear|tenga after langoy|otitis externa mild|masakit tenga after swim
display_name: Mild swimmer's ear
tip_1: Keep the ear dry; avoid swimming until comfortable.
tip_2: Do not insert buds or tip liquids deep into the canal unless a clinician advised drops.
tip_3: Wipe only the outer ear; tilt the head to drain water after showers.
tip_4: Pain may ease with a warm compress outside the ear.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for increasing pain, discharge, fever, swelling around the ear, or diabetes — outer-ear infection may need prescribed drops.

aliases: itchy nose|hapong ilong|kati ilong|allergic nose itch
display_name: Itchy allergic nose
tip_1: Saline rinse/spray can clear allergens from the nose.
tip_2: Avoid rubbing/upward nose wiping that worsens irritation.
tip_3: Wash bedding and reduce dust exposure in the bedroom.
tip_4: Ask about non-sedating antihistamines if symptoms persist and are suitable for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for breathing difficulty, wheezing, or facial swelling.

aliases: stye|kuliti|hordeolum|pigsa sa talukap
display_name: Early stye
tip_1: Apply a clean warm compress to the closed eyelid 5–10 minutes, several times a day.
tip_2: Do not squeeze the stye.
tip_3: Avoid eye makeup and contact lenses until resolved.
tip_4: Wash hands before any eyelid care.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if vision changes, the whole eyelid swells shut, fever develops, or it worsens after 1–2 days.

aliases: callus|callous|ipak|corn foot|matigas balat paa
display_name: Mild callus / corn
tip_1: Soak and gently file thickened skin — do not cut with blades at home.
tip_2: Use cushioned pads and better-fitting shoes to reduce pressure.
tip_3: Moisturize surrounding skin; keep the area clean.
tip_4: Never share foot blades or try deep cutting.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you have diabetes, poor circulation, or the area becomes red, warm, or painful.

aliases: nappy thrush|diaper yeast|pulang lampin yeast|candidal diaper
display_name: Suspected diaper yeast rash
tip_1: Change diapers often; allow short air-dry time.
tip_2: Keep the area clean with water; pat dry fully including skin folds.
tip_3: Barrier cream helps irritation; yeast rashes often need antifungal cream advised by a clinician/pharmacist.
tip_4: Wash hands after each change.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the rash has satellite spots that worsen, with fever, or open sores.

aliases: pregnancy backache|sakit likod buntis|prenatal back pain mild
display_name: Mild pregnancy backache
tip_1: Use a pregnancy pillow or side-lying with pillow support between knees.
tip_2: Practice gentle pelvic tilts and short walks if your clinician allows.
tip_3: Avoid heavy lifting and high heels.
tip_4: Warm (not hot) compress on the back may comfort — avoid prolonged high heat on the belly.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for back pain with bleeding, fluid leak, contractions, fever, or leg weakness — report new symptoms to your maternity clinician.

aliases: sore nipples breastfeed|masakit utong padede|latch pain mild
display_name: Mild breastfeeding nipple soreness
tip_1: Check latch with a lactation-trained nurse/midwife when possible — poor latch is a common cause.
tip_2: Apply a little expressed milk to the nipple and air-dry after feeds if advised.
tip_3: Start feeds on the less-sore side; ensure baby opens wide.
tip_4: Avoid harsh soaps on nipples.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for fever, breast redness/heat (possible mastitis), cracked bleeding nipples, or severe pain.

aliases: travel anxiety mild|takot byahe|nervous travel|kabado sa biyahe
display_name: Mild travel nerves
tip_1: Prepare a simple bag checklist the night before to reduce rush stress.
tip_2: Use slow breathing during boarding or traffic waits.
tip_3: Limit excess caffeine before travel.
tip_4: Distract with music or a short walk if safe at stops.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent help for panic with chest pain, fainting, or thoughts of self-harm.

aliases: low mood mild|malungkot mild|down days|mild sadness
display_name: Mild low mood self-care
tip_1: Keep a basic routine: wake time, short walk, and one small achievable task.
tip_2: Stay connected to a trusted friend or family member.
tip_3: Limit alcohol; protect sleep and regular meals.
tip_4: Write worries down to revisit later rather than looping all night.
when_to_seek_care: Seek help promptly for hopelessness, self-harm thoughts, or inability to function — call local crisis lines / emergency services if in danger.

aliases: hip pain|sakit balakang|masakit ang balakang|hip ache mild
display_name: Mild hip pain
tip_1: Avoid long sitting without breaks; stand and walk briefly every 30–60 minutes.
tip_2: Use a warm compress for stiffness or brief ice after aggravating activity.
tip_3: Sleep on the less painful side with a pillow between the knees if helpful.
tip_4: Gentle hip stretches within comfort; avoid deep squats while sore.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care after a fall, inability to bear weight, fever with hip pain, or pain shooting with numbness.
resource_label: NHS: Sprains and strains / joint pain

aliases: calf strain|sakit binti after takbo|pulled calf|masakit betis
display_name: Mild calf strain
tip_1: Rest from running/jumping for a few days; walk as tolerated.
tip_2: Ice briefly with a cloth barrier in the first 1–2 days if swollen.
tip_3: Gentle ankle pumps and calf stretches once sharp pain eases.
tip_4: Supportive shoes and gradual return to activity reduce re-injury.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden pop with severe swelling, inability to walk, or one-sided calf heat/redness (possible clot risk).

aliases: shin splints|sakit shin|sakit harapan binti|medial tibial pain mild
display_name: Mild shin splints
tip_1: Reduce high-impact running for several days; switch to walking or cycling if pain-free.
tip_2: Ice the shins briefly after activity.
tip_3: Check shoe cushioning; avoid sudden mileage jumps.
tip_4: Calf stretches and soft-surface walking can help recovery.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for focal bone pain at rest, swelling after trauma, or pain that worsens despite rest.
resource_label: NHS: Sprains and strains / joint pain

aliases: arch pain|sakit arko paa|flat feet ache|masakit loob talampakan
display_name: Mild foot arch pain
tip_1: Rest from long standing; elevate feet after work.
tip_2: Supportive shoes or over-the-counter arch inserts may help if they fit well.
tip_3: Gentle towel-scrunch foot exercises and calf stretches within comfort.
tip_4: Avoid barefoot on hard floors while symptomatic.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you have diabetes with foot wounds, sudden swelling, or cannot walk.
resource_label: NHS: Sprains and strains / joint pain

aliases: thumb sprain mild|sakit hinlalaki|gamekeeper mild|masakit thumb
display_name: Mild thumb strain
tip_1: Rest from gripping and texting marathons for 24–48 hours.
tip_2: Ice briefly if swollen; buddy-tape only if taught and sensation stays normal.
tip_3: Keep fingers moving gently to avoid stiffness.
tip_4: Return to lifting gradually with a neutral wrist/thumb position.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for visible deformity, numbness, or inability to pinch after injury.

aliases: jammed finger|nasaktan daliri|finger sprain mild|swollen finger mild
display_name: Mild jammed finger
tip_1: Buddy-tape to the neighboring finger if alignment looks normal and you were taught how.
tip_2: Ice briefly and elevate the hand.
tip_3: Remove rings early before swelling increases.
tip_4: Gentle motion after 24 hours if pain allows.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for crooked finger, open wound, numbness, or inability to straighten/bend.

aliases: tailbone pain|sakit puwit buto|coccyx pain|sakit coccyx
display_name: Mild tailbone pain
tip_1: Use a donut cushion or lean forward slightly when sitting.
tip_2: Apply ice or warmth in short sessions as comfortable.
tip_3: Avoid long hard-bench sitting; stand and walk breaks help.
tip_4: Stool softeners via fiber/water reduce pain from constipation straining.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care after major fall, numbness in the saddle area, or bowel/bladder changes.
resource_label: NHS: Sprains, strains and joint pain

aliases: chest muscle strain|sakit dibdib kalamnan|pulled chest muscle|masakit dibdib after ehersisyo
display_name: Mild chest-wall muscle strain
tip_1: Rest from push-ups/heavy lifting for a few days.
tip_2: Warm compress and gentle arm circles within pain limits.
tip_3: Support the area when coughing if sore.
tip_4: Return to exercise gradually once pain-free at rest.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for pressure-like chest pain, sweating, shortness of breath, or pain spreading to jaw/arm — rule out heart causes first.
resource_label: NHS: Sprains and strains / joint pain

aliases: gas colic|sakit tiyan kabag|colicky gas|masakit tiyan with gas
display_name: Mild gas colic
tip_1: Walk after meals; avoid gulping drinks and straws for a day.
tip_2: Apply a warm compress to the abdomen.
tip_3: Reduce gas-forming foods temporarily if they are known triggers.
tip_4: Simethicone-style products may help some adults if labeled for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe progressive pain, vomiting, fever, or rigid abdomen.

aliases: travel constipation|hirap tumae byahe|constipated on trip
display_name: Travel constipation
tip_1: Drink extra water on travel days; pack fiber-rich snacks if suitable.
tip_2: Keep a walking routine at stops; do not ignore the urge to go.
tip_3: Choose familiar foods when possible; limit heavy dehydrating alcohol.
tip_4: Ask a pharmacist about gentle options if needed and appropriate for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for severe pain, vomiting, or no stool for several days with bloating.

aliases: nausea after medicine|sumerko gamot|medicine upset stomach
display_name: Mild medicine-related nausea
tip_1: Take the medicine with food if the label/clinician allows.
tip_2: Sip water slowly; rest upright after doses.
tip_3: Do not double the next dose if you vomited — ask a pharmacist/clinician.
tip_4: Keep a list of which medicines trigger nausea.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for vomiting blood, rash/swelling after a dose, breathing trouble, or persistent vomiting.

aliases: sore tongue|sakit dila|burning tongue mild|masakit dila
display_name: Mild sore tongue
tip_1: Avoid very hot, acidic, or spicy foods until healed.
tip_2: Rinse with warm salt water; stay hydrated.
tip_3: Use a soft toothbrush; avoid alcohol mouthwashes that sting.
tip_4: Note if a sharp tooth edge is cutting the tongue.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for white patches that do not wipe off, sores >2 weeks, swelling that affects breathing, or unexplained weight loss.

aliases: bad breath|halitosis|mabahong hininga|foul breath mild
display_name: Mild bad breath (hygiene)
tip_1: Brush twice daily including the tongue; floss once daily.
tip_2: Stay hydrated; dry mouth worsens odor.
tip_3: Replace an old toothbrush and clean dentures/retainers daily if used.
tip_4: Limit smoking and strong-odor foods before important talks.
when_to_seek_care: See a dentist/clinician if odor persists with tooth pain, gum swelling, or sinus infection signs.

aliases: dry mouth|tuyong bibig|xerostomia|walang laway
display_name: Dry mouth
tip_1: Sip water often; chew sugar-free gum if appropriate to stimulate saliva.
tip_2: Use a humidifier at night if air is dry.
tip_3: Avoid alcohol mouthwashes and limit caffeine/alcohol which dry the mouth.
tip_4: Ask a pharmacist about saliva substitutes if needed.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if dry mouth is sudden with facial swelling, cannot swallow, or follows new medicine with severe symptoms.

aliases: dry nose|tuyong ilong|crusty nose|ilong bitak
display_name: Dry nasal passages
tip_1: Use saline spray or gel to moisturize the nose.
tip_2: Run a clean humidifier; avoid picking dried crusts.
tip_3: Limit prolonged direct AC/fan on the face while sleeping.
tip_4: A thin layer of plain ointment at the nostril rim may help outer dryness — do not pack grease deep inside.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for frequent nosebleeds, severe pain, or foul discharge.

aliases: dry throat|tuyong lalamunan|scratchy dry throat
display_name: Dry throat
tip_1: Drink water regularly; limit mouth-breathing when possible.
tip_2: Use mild steam or a humidifier overnight.
tip_3: Honey in warm water may soothe adults/older children (not infants).
tip_4: Avoid smoke and very dry air exposure.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you cannot swallow liquids, have high fever, or breathing difficulty.

aliases: voice strain|pagod boses|teacher voice|paos after talking
display_name: Voice overuse strain
tip_1: Rest the voice; avoid shouting and whispering.
tip_2: Sip water often; humidify dry rooms.
tip_3: Use amplification rather than projecting loudly when possible.
tip_4: Warm up gently before long speaking days.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if hoarseness lasts >2–3 weeks or you have breathing trouble/coughing blood.
resource_label: NHS: Sprains and strains / joint pain

aliases: dust mite allergy|hapong alikabok|allergy unan|dust allergy home
display_name: Dust-mite allergy home care
tip_1: Wash bedding weekly in hot water when possible; use allergen covers if available.
tip_2: Vacuum mattresses/floors regularly; reduce clutter that collects dust.
tip_3: Keep humidity moderated; fix damp areas that grow mites/mold.
tip_4: Saline rinse and labeled antihistamines may help if suitable.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for wheezing, chest tightness, or severe facial swelling.

aliases: pet allergy|hapong aso pusa|cat allergy mild|dog dander allergy
display_name: Pet dander allergy
tip_1: Keep pets out of the bedroom if possible; wash hands after petting.
tip_2: Vacuum and dust often; bathe pets as recommended by a vet when helpful.
tip_3: HEPA filtration may reduce airborne dander indoors.
tip_4: Ask about antihistamines if appropriate for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for asthma-like breathing trouble or anaphylaxis signs.

aliases: mold irritation|hapong amag|moldy smell symptoms|amag allergy mild
display_name: Mild mold irritation
tip_1: Increase ventilation; fix leaks and dry damp walls/ceilings.
tip_2: Clean small hard-surface mold with proper protection; leave large areas to professionals.
tip_3: Wash soft items that smell musty; reduce indoor humidity.
tip_4: Saline rinse can ease irritated nose/throat.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for worsening asthma, fever with cough after heavy exposure, or severe breathing symptoms.

aliases: smoke irritation|hapong usok|usok ubo|irritation from smoke
display_name: Smoke / haze irritation
tip_1: Stay indoors with windows closed during heavy smoke when possible.
tip_2: Use a mask rated for particles if you must go outside.
tip_3: Rinse eyes with clean water; saline for the nose.
tip_4: Drink fluids; rest if coughing from irritation.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or symptoms in infants/elderly that worsen.

aliases: chlorine eyes|mata after swimming|pool eye burn mild|irritated eyes pool
display_name: Pool / chlorine eye irritation
tip_1: Rinse eyes with clean fresh water after swimming.
tip_2: Use lubricating drops if suitable; rest contact lenses until comfortable.
tip_3: Avoid rubbing.
tip_4: Swim goggles prevent repeat irritation.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for vision loss, severe pain, chemical splash of non-pool chemicals, or light sensitivity lasting days.

aliases: sweat rash|init-init|prickly heat|bungang araw|heat rash
display_name: Heat rash / prickly heat
tip_1: Move to a cooler place; wear loose cotton clothing.
tip_2: Keep skin clean and dry; avoid thick greasy creams that block pores.
tip_3: Cool showers help; do not scrub raw areas.
tip_4: Calamine may ease itch if appropriate.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for pus, fever, spreading redness, or rash in infants that looks severe.

aliases: chafing|gasgas hita|thigh rub|skin rub rash
display_name: Skin chafing
tip_1: Keep the area clean and dry; apply a plain barrier ointment if unbroken.
tip_2: Wear moisture-wicking or better-fitting clothes; consider shorts liners for long walks.
tip_3: Reduce friction activities until skin calms.
tip_4: Avoid fragranced products that sting open skin.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the skin breaks open widely, shows pus, or you have diabetes with groin/foot chafing wounds.

aliases: ingrown hair|talo buhok|ingrown shave bump|razor bump
display_name: Ingrown hair / razor bump
tip_1: Stop shaving the area briefly; warm compresses may help a bump surface.
tip_2: Do not dig with needles.
tip_3: Exfoliate gently only on intact skin; use clean razors and shave with the grain when you resume.
tip_4: Wear loose clothing over the area.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for expanding redness, fever, or painful boils.

aliases: ingrown toenail|kuko tumusok|ingrown nail early|sakit kuko paa
display_name: Early ingrown toenail
tip_1: Soak the foot in warm water; keep the area clean and dry afterward.
tip_2: Wear roomy shoes; avoid tight socks.
tip_3: Do not cut deep nail spikes yourself.
tip_4: A small piece of clean cotton under a mild edge may help some early cases — stop if pain worsens.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for pus, spreading redness, fever, or if you have diabetes — do not delay foot infections.

aliases: hangnail|bitak kuko|torn cuticle|sakit gilid kuko
display_name: Hangnail / torn cuticle
tip_1: Trim carefully with clean nail scissors — do not rip.
tip_2: Apply a plain ointment and a bandage if the skin is open.
tip_3: Moisturize cuticles regularly; avoid harsh nail chemicals.
tip_4: Keep nails clean and short.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if redness spreads up the finger, with pus or fever (possible paronychia).

aliases: paper cut|hiwa papel|small paper wound
display_name: Paper cut
tip_1: Wash with soap and water.
tip_2: Apply light pressure if bleeding.
tip_3: Use a thin bandage to reduce sting and dirt entry.
tip_4: Antibiotic ointment is optional for clean minor cuts if suitable.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the cut is deep, on the face, or shows infection signs.

aliases: splinter under nail|tinik sa kuko|wood under nail
display_name: Splinter under nail
tip_1: Soak to soften; try clean tweezers only on a visible tip.
tip_2: Do not force deep digging under the nail.
tip_3: Keep the finger clean and covered.
tip_4: Watch for throbbing pain or pus.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if you cannot remove it, pain is severe, or infection signs appear — especially for dirty/rusty material.

aliases: fishbone feeling|tinik isda lalamunan|bone stuck throat mild
display_name: Possible fishbone throat sensation
tip_1: Stop eating solid dry boluses that could push a bone deeper.
tip_2: Sip water; soft bread is sometimes tried but do not force if pain is sharp.
tip_3: Do not try to dig with fingers.
tip_4: Note if you can swallow saliva and breathe normally.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care if you feel something stuck with pain, drooling, breathing trouble, or vomiting blood — get clinical exam/imaging if needed.

aliases: insect in ear|may insekto sa tenga|bug in ear
display_name: Insect in ear
tip_1: Tilt the affected ear down; do not poke with buds.
tip_2: If the insect is visible at the opening, gentle light may encourage exit outdoors — do not pour random oils if the eardrum may be damaged.
tip_3: Stay calm to avoid pushing it deeper.
tip_4: Seek clinic care promptly for safe removal.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for severe pain, bleeding, dizziness, or hearing loss.

aliases: something in eye|may idek sa mata|foreign body eye mild|buhangin sa mata
display_name: Foreign body in eye (mild)
tip_1: Do not rub. Blink repeatedly and rinse with clean water or saline.
tip_2: Pull the upper lid over the lower lid gently to sweep particles.
tip_3: Remove contact lenses.
tip_4: Avoid cotton buds on the eye surface.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for chemicals, metal/glass, vision loss, or if the particle will not rinse out.

aliases: sun glare headache|sakit ulo araw|glare headache
display_name: Sun-glare headache
tip_1: Move to shade; rest your eyes from bright light.
tip_2: Wear sunglasses outdoors; drink water.
tip_3: A cool cloth on the forehead may help.
tip_4: Labeled OTC pain relief may help if suitable for you.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden worst headache, vision loss, neck stiffness, or headache after head injury.

aliases: caffeine withdrawal|sakit ulo walang kape|coffee headache
display_name: Caffeine withdrawal headache
tip_1: Hydrate and rest in a quiet space.
tip_2: A smaller than usual caffeine dose may ease withdrawal if appropriate for you — then taper gradually later.
tip_3: Eat a light meal; gentle walk can help.
tip_4: Keep a steady daily caffeine pattern to prevent swings.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if headache is sudden/severe with neurological warning signs.

aliases: tech neck|sakit leeg cellphone|text neck|leeg after phone
display_name: Phone / screen neck strain
tip_1: Raise the phone/screen toward eye level; take posture breaks every 20–30 minutes.
tip_2: Gentle neck side-bends and chin tucks within comfort.
tip_3: Warm compress for tight muscles.
tip_4: Strengthen upper back with simple scapular squeezes if pain-free.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for arm numbness/weakness, severe pain after trauma, or fever with stiff neck.

aliases: eye twitch|kumikislap mata|eyelid twitch|myokymia mild
display_name: Mild eyelid twitch
tip_1: Rest your eyes; reduce caffeine and improve sleep for a few days.
tip_2: Apply a warm compress to the lid.
tip_3: Limit screen strain with the 20-20-20 rule.
tip_4: Most twitches settle on their own.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care if the whole side of the face droops, the eye will not close, or twitching lasts many weeks.

aliases: sensitive teeth|ngilo|ngilo ngipin|cold sensitive tooth
display_name: Tooth sensitivity
tip_1: Use a desensitizing toothpaste as labeled for 2+ weeks.
tip_2: Avoid very cold/hot extremes and acidic sodas for a while.
tip_3: Brush gently with a soft brush; do not scrub at the gumline.
tip_4: A night guard may help if you grind teeth — ask a dentist.
when_to_seek_care: See a dentist for sharp pain on one tooth, swelling, or sensitivity after trauma.

aliases: wisdom tooth pain|sakit Cordales|sakit third molar mild|masakit bungi likod
display_name: Mild wisdom-tooth ache
tip_1: Rinse with warm salt water after meals to clear food traps.
tip_2: Soft foods and labeled OTC pain relief if suitable.
tip_3: Keep the area clean with gentle brushing.
tip_4: Cold pack outside the jaw may ease swelling comfort.
when_to_seek_care: Seek dental care for facial swelling, fever, trouble opening the mouth, or pain that wakes you at night.

aliases: braces pain|sakit braces|ortho wire poke|masakit ngipin braces
display_name: Braces / orthodontic soreness
tip_1: Eat soft foods for 1–2 days after adjustments.
tip_2: Orthodontic wax on poking wires can help.
tip_3: Warm salt rinses soothe sore gums.
tip_4: Labeled OTC pain relief may help if suitable.
when_to_seek_care: Call your orthodontist for a loose bracket, long wire stabbing the cheek, or severe swelling.

aliases: period bloating|kabag regla|bloated period|mabuntis feeling regla
display_name: Period bloating
tip_1: Reduce salty snacks briefly; sip water steadily rather than large sodas.
tip_2: Light walking eases gas and fluid discomfort for many people.
tip_3: Warm compress on the lower abdomen.
tip_4: Track whether bloating is typical for your cycle.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for sudden severe pain, fainting, or bloating unlike your usual periods.

aliases: period fatigue|pagod regla|tired on period
display_name: Period-related tiredness
tip_1: Rest extra on heavy days; keep iron-rich foods in meals if your diet allows.
tip_2: Hydrate and avoid skipping meals.
tip_3: Light movement often helps more than total bed rest.
tip_4: Labeled OTC pain relief for cramps may improve sleep if suitable.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for very heavy soaking bleeding, dizziness on standing, or fainting.

aliases: yeast itch mild|kati private mild|candidiasis itch mild|hapong private mild
display_name: Mild genital itch (possible yeast)
tip_1: Wear cotton underwear; avoid tight synthetic clothes for a few days.
tip_2: Do not douche; wash with water only externally.
tip_3: Avoid scented soaps and pads if they irritate.
tip_4: Pharmacy antifungal treatments exist but confirm fit with a clinician/pharmacist if unsure or recurrent.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for first-time symptoms, pelvic pain, fever, foul discharge, pregnancy, or symptoms in children/males.

aliases: hot flash|init menopause|night sweat mild|hot flush
display_name: Mild hot flashes
tip_1: Dress in layers; keep a small fan or cool water nearby.
tip_2: Limit alcohol, spicy meals, and late caffeine if they trigger you.
tip_3: Cool the bedroom; use moisture-wicking sleepwear.
tip_4: Pace stress with slow breathing during a flush.
when_to_seek_care: Seek care for chest pain with flushes, very heavy bleeding, or symptoms that disrupt life — discuss options with a clinician.

aliases: pregnancy heartburn|asido buntis|acid while pregnant
display_name: Pregnancy heartburn
tip_1: Eat smaller meals; stay upright after eating.
tip_2: Elevate the head of the bed slightly at night.
tip_3: Avoid known triggers (very fatty/spicy late meals).
tip_4: Ask your maternity clinician/pharmacist before any antacid — some are preferred in pregnancy.
when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent care for chest pressure with shortness of breath, or severe vomiting.

aliases: pregnancy leg cramp|pulikat buntis|leg cramp pregnant
